pp:me:2002:q9.title: GATE ME 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 9
pp:me:2002:q9.question: The minimum number of links in a single degree-of-freedom planar mechanism with both higher and lower kinematic pairs is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: A planar mechanism has both lower and higher kinematic pairs and is of single degree of freedom. Formula used (Kutzbach criterion for planar mechanisms): $F = 3(L - 1) - 2J_1 - J_2$ Where, F = degree of freedom L = number of links J1 = number of lower pairs J2 = number of higher pairs For single degree of freedom: $F = 1$ Assume minimum possible number of links: $L = 4$ Substitute values: $1 = 3(4 - 1) - 2J_1 - J_2$ $1 = 9 - 2J_1 - J_2$ $2J_1 + J_2 = 8$ This equation can be satisfied with a valid combination of lower and higher pairs. Therefore, minimum number of links = 4

Boundary layer thickness,

$\delta=\frac{5 x}{\sqrt{\mathrm{Re}_{x}}}$ for laminor boundary layer

pp:me:2002:q31.title: GATE ME 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 31
pp:me:2002:q31.question: A project consists of three parallel paths with mean durations and variances of (10,4), (12,4) and (12,9) respectively. According to the standard PERT assumptions, the distribution of the project duration is
options: Beta with mean 10 and standard deviation 2
Beta with mean 12 and standard deviation 2
Normal with mean 10 and standard deviation 3
Normal with mean 12 and standard deviation 3

detailed_solution.markdown:
In PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique), it is assumed that:

:

The project duration is governed by the critical path (the longest expected duration among all paths).

The project duration follows a normal distribution approximately, due to the Central Limit Theorem.

Step 1: List the mean durations and variances for each path:

Path 1: $\mu_1 = 10, \ \sigma_1^2 = 4$

Path 2: $\mu_2 = 12, \ \sigma_2^2 = 4$

Path 3: $\mu_3 = 12, \ \sigma_3^2 = 9$

Step 2: Identify the critical path

Since the critical path is the one with the maximum mean duration:

$\max(\mu_1, \mu_2, \mu_3) = \max(10, 12, 12) = 12$

We have two paths with mean duration 12.

As per PERT, among these, the path with the larger variance is considered for total project variance (more conservative estimate).

Thus, select Path 3:

$\mu = 12, \ \sigma^2 = 9$

Step 3: Write the distribution

The project duration approximately follows a normal distribution:

$N(\mu, \sigma^2)$

i.e.,

$N(12, 9)$

Or equivalently:

Mean = 12, Standard Deviation = $\sqrt{9} = 3$.

pp:me:2002:q45.title: GATE ME 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 45
pp:me:2002:q45.question:
The properties of mercury at 300 K are: density = 13529 $kg/m^{3}$,  specific heat at constant pressure = 0.1393 kJ/kg-K,  dynamic viscosity = $0.1523\times 10^{-2} N.s/m^{2}$
 and thermal conductivity =8.540 W/m-K. The Prandtl number of the mercury at 300 K is

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Free and Forced Convection
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \rho &=13529 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ c_{p} &=0.1393 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ &=139.3 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \mu &=0.1523 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Ns} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ k_{f} &=8.540 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \end{aligned}$$

Prandtl number,

$$\begin{aligned} P r &=\frac{\mu C_{p}}{k_{f}} \\ &=\frac{0.1523 \times 10^{-2} \times 139.3}{8.540} \\ &=0.0248 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2002:q46.title: GATE ME 2002 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:me:2002:q46.question: What is the value of the view factor for two inclined flat hving common edge of equal width, and with an angle of 20 degrees?

detailed_solution.markdown: Let l be the length of both plates and assumed that surrounding between two large plate be as surface 3. $$\begin{aligned} A_{1} &=A_{2} \\ F_{11}+F_{12}+F_{13} &=0 \; \; \; \left(F_{11}=0\right) \\ F_{21}+F_{22}+F_{23} &=1 \; \; \; \left(F_{22}=0\right) \\ F_{31}+F_{32}+F_{33} &=1 \; \; \; \left(F_{33}=0\right) \\ \text{By symmetry }F_{31}&=F_{32} \\ 2 F_{31}&=2 F_{32}=1 \\ F_{31} &=F_{32}=0.5 \\ A_{1} F_{13} &=A_{3} F_{31} \times \l \times w) \times F_{13} \\&=\left(2 l \sin 10^{\circ} \times w\right) \times 0.5 \\ F_{13} &=\sin 10^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$ By cosine law $$\begin{aligned} b^{2} &=l^{2}+l^{2}-2 l^{2} \cos 20^{\circ} \\ \Rightarrow \quad b^{2} &=2 l^{2}\left(1-\cos 20^{\circ}\right) \\ &=2 l^{2} \times 2 \sin ^{2} 10^{\circ} \\ &=4 l^{2} \sin ^{2} 10^{\circ} \\ b &=2 l \sin 10^{\circ} \\ F_{12} &=1-F_{13}=1-\sin 10^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$ By symmetry $$\begin{aligned} F_{12} &=F_{21}=1-\sin 10^{\circ} \\ &=0.826 \end{aligned}$$ Alternatively: $$\begin{aligned} F_{12} &=F_{21}=1-\sin \frac{\theta}{2} \\ &=1-\sin \left(\frac{20^{\circ}}{2}\right)=0.826 \end{aligned}$$
